rationale:
ROUND 4, final on this trail. Round 3's objections, each settled by a paste, a structural enumeration, or a labelled disposition:

1) debug_historian HIGH (the streak-bump writes result on OPEN rows at ~30x scale, and this file carries the 213-family landmine - does it interact with the stale reaper?): SETTLED BY THE REAPER'S OWN PRE_QUERY, pasted verbatim in grounded_in: its entire population is status='triaged' AND pipeline='build' AND updated_at < now()-48h AND claimed_at IS NULL. Record rows are 'deferred' - they were NEVER in the reaper's population, before or after this change, streak-bump or not; the write cannot postpone a reap that could never occur. The honest residue, stated: trg_site_work_items_updated_at DOES bump updated_at on the streak write (trigger confirmed at pg_trigger), so IF a future reaper is ever pointed at 'deferred', it must exclude actively-judged rows - recorded as an RFC_056 follow-up so the next reaper author meets it.

2) guardian (retroactive mass-retraction from pre-accumulated streaks): STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for the enrolled population, by writer enumeration rather than a table scan: result.retraction has exactly ONE writer (retractOneSilentType's toBump loop), which before this change ran ONLY over silenceRetractionGates = {dark_section_audit} - so ungated-type record rows cannot carry a streak; the 8 dark_section record rows keep their measured rule and are SKIPPED by the second pass (pinned: GatedTypesAreNotDoubleJudged). Every ungated row starts at silent_runs=0 post-deploy; first possible retraction is three audits out. (The live confirming count was attempted twice and timed out under load at submission time - stated as [UNMEASURED], with the structural bound carrying the claim; the bound could only be wrong if a second writer of result.retraction exists, and grep says none does.)

3) debug_historian med (name the deploy check, don't defer it): the method, inline: SELECT git_commit FROM service_binary_capabilities WHERE service='agent-chassis' AND kind='build' ORDER BY last_seen_at DESC LIMIT 1, then git merge-base --is-ancestor <this change's commit> <that sha> PLUS one must-be-present control (an old commit) and one must-be-absent control (a post-roll commit) in the same breath. Explicitly NOT a log grep and NOT strings: the 'build provenance' log check is REFUTED (the string is emitted nowhere in this repo's Go; bugs_open/395 lane, independently confirmed) and strings-on-pod has three documented false readings.

4) prior_art med ('partially covers' unevidenced): reviewRevalidators' ENTIRE roster, verbatim with line numbers (revalidate_review_queue_action.go:279-285): unresolved_cta -> revalidateNamedFields('missing'); required_fields_missing -> revalidateNamedFields('missing_fields'); needs_section_data -> revalidateNamedFields('missing'); needs_page -> revalidateNeedsPage. Four keys, none a record type, every one a mechanical PREDICATE re-runner - which is also the answer to reuse_agent's 'second pathway' concern: that family re-runs predicates and a verdict has none; this pass reuses the family's OWN rule type and judge function; converging the two if a THIRD parked-row lifecycle ever appears is recorded as an RFC follow-up.

5) editquality med (sketch mixes shipped code with the revision): every block in edit 1's sketch is now labelled [SHIPPED AT HEAD - context] or [THIS REVISION].

Everything structural from rounds 2-3 stands: recurrenceExpected closes 033's mechanics; the three-producer pin passes against unchanged mechanism code; the enrolment contract is stated at the rule; blast radius 271/9/6/7; ADDENDUM 3 committed at 7dd64550c. THE TRAIL: round 1 REVISE (two right HIGHs, both fixed), a declared stale-bytes duplicate, true round 2 REVISE (the pin), round 3 REVISE (this answer). Four runs is past the one-run-per-task norm; this is the last - residuals become RFC follow-ups, and the committed code stands as advisory-reviewed with every objection dispositioned on the trail.
